task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req174-wasm-instance-pooling-or-decline.md or similar) for REQ-174. Step 1: make an explicit, justified ADOPT or DECLINE decision on instance pooling, live-verifying wasmex's actual pooling support (if any) in the installed dependency version before deciding -- do not decide in the abstract. If DECLINE: the design must state the reason (e.g. the current per-invocation-fresh-instance pattern already shipped in ModuleVersionRegistry.invoke/4 and PluginHandler.run_guest/3 already gives isolation-by-construction with no residue risk, so pooling's amortization benefit doesn't currently justify the isolation risk decision 0014 (e) flags) and specify the test(s) that assert per-invocation isolation holds regardless (data written to guest memory in invocation N is not observable in invocation N+1 of the same module) -- this must be a REAL, concrete test design, not just an assertion that isolation is 'obviously' true because instances are fresh. If ADOPT: the design must specify the pooling mechanism (checkout/return-to-pool lifecycle), the exact memory-reset mechanism and WHERE it is enforced (by construction -- e.g. reset happens unconditionally before an instance re-enters the pool, even on a failed/trapped invocation, not merely 'expected to happen'), how a pooled instance of a module version superseded by REQ-173's activate/2 is prevented from ever being handed to a new invocation (this must compose with ModuleVersionRegistry's existing checkout/ref-count mechanism, not duplicate or conflict with it), and the benchmark methodology for WASM-13's own p50-latency acceptance criterion recorded as a moduledoc/design-artefact number, explicitly NOT as a CI-gated test threshold. Either way, the design must state explicitly that this restates WASM-13 by ADDING the per-invocation memory-reset correctness constraint (absent from WASM-13's original text) and cite decision 0014 (e) plus the wasmex Store-reuse behavior motivating it. Design only -- no implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: the moduledoc records an explicit decision: pooling adopted, or pooling declined with its reason -- WASM-13 is a SHOULD and declining is legitimate, but silence is not
a test asserts per-invocation isolation regardless of which way the decision went: data written to guest memory in invocation N is NOT observable in invocation N+1 of the same module

if pooling is adopted, a test asserts memory reset happens between invocations by construction -- e.g. an invocation that fails or traps mid-write still leaves no residue for the next invocation -- and the moduledoc states this is a correctness requirement per decision 0014's restatement, not a performance detail
if pooling is adopted, a test asserts a pooled instance of a module version superseded by REQ-173's activation is never handed to a new invocation
if pooling is adopted, WASM-13's p50 latency comparison is recorded as a benchmark with real measured numbers quoted in the moduledoc or a design artefact; no CI test asserts a latency threshold

the moduledoc states that this requirement restates WASM-13 by ADDING the per-invocation memory-reset correctness constraint, which is absent from WASM-13's original text, and cites decision 0014 (e) and the wasmex Store-reuse behaviour that motivates it
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
